root_motivation: Grounding: fleet board dogfood, 2026-09-30 -- host.channel.open(name: "fleet") returned id 01M3V2YTK8F0TF96KX6Q29T08Z; host.channel.post on that id succeeded; host.channel.read on the same id failed "no channel found for that name or id", reproduced three times running. post (src/channels.rs) already tried a group-channel lookup then fell back to the named-channel id-or-name lookup (src/db.rs); read ran only the group lookup, so a channel opened by name -- the first form host.channel.open's own doc comment documents -- was writable and unreadable. freeze/close had the same narrower, group-only reach. This build gives every host.channel.* verb (open excepted, since its own group vs name argument already disambiguates what it creates) one resolve_channel(tenant, key) lookup in channels.rs, so a channel reachable by one verb is reachable by every other one too.
user_persona: An agent that opens a channel by name (the first form host.channel.open documents) and expects post/read/freeze/close to all resolve that same name or id -- the fleet board's own alert-verification loop was blocked exactly here. Also an agent that mistypes a key and needs the error to say what lookups were tried, and the operator, who needs freeze/close to work identically on a named or a group channel for moderation to hold.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given host.channel.open(name: "t") returning id X, When host.channel.post(X, body) then host.channel.read(X) run, Then read returns the post with seq 1 and a next_cursor.
Given the same channel, When host.channel.read("t") runs by name, Then it returns the same posts.
Given a group channel, When read, post, freeze, close run as before this PRD, Then results are byte-identical to the pre-PRD fixtures (no regression).
Given a nonexistent key, When any channel verb runs, Then the error class is channel_not_found, data.key echoes the input, and the message names both lookups.

Given a named channel, When freeze(X) then post(X, ...) run, Then post fails channel_frozen; When close(X) then read(X), Then read still works (closed channels stay readable, matching errors.rs's documented rule).
Given tools/list, When fetched, Then host.channel.open's description names both channel kinds and says both are readable.

scope: src/channels.rs: resolve_channel(state, tenant, key) (requirement 1) -- group lookup by id first, then the named-channel id-or-name lookup, returning a ResolvedChannel{channel_id, kind: Group|Named, owner_tenant_id, group_name, closed_at, frozen_at}; open/post/read/close/freeze/unfreeze all route through it instead of each keeping a private lookup.

src/db.rs: channel_named_lookup, the named-channel counterpart to the existing channel_group_lookup, selecting closed_at/frozen_at off the channels row so post/read/freeze/close/unfreeze all see the same two columns regardless of channel kind; channel_group_set_flag's UPDATE WHERE clause extended to also match a named channel owned (channels.created_by) by the caller, the missing owner-side half AC5 needs.

src/errors.rs: AppError::channel_not_found(key) now takes the caller's key, carries it as data.key, and names both lookups it tried, replacing the old static "name or id" message that named a lookup read never actually ran.

src/handler.rs: host.channel.open/post/read/close/freeze/unfreeze tool descriptions (tools/list) state that both a named and a group channel exist and are both fully readable, since read/close/freeze/unfreeze now reach a named channel too.

additional.test_file_names_use_underscores_not_the_: test_prefix chanread (the PRD's own frontmatter field), same convention as every other test file in this repo.
additional.version_bump_patch: PRD frontmatter build_version_bump: patch -- Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock/plugin.json bumped 0.65.0 -> 0.65.1, landed with AC6.
additional.no_schema_change: PRD's own migration/compatibility section: no schema change, existing named channels become readable; routing only, not new queries (PRD's own technical considerations).
additional.named_channel_readers_are_owner_only: PRD's own technical considerations, drafted: a named channel's readers are its owner only -- a non-owner's read gets channel_not_found, identical in shape to a miss (AC4's own parity requirement), not a separate authorization error class.
additional.post_no_longer_auto_advances_the_poster_: Landed with AC1 as a necessary side effect, not a separate requirement: channel_post previously advanced the poster's own channel_cursors row on insert, which made a poster's own post invisible to the poster's own very next read -- the opposite of this PRD's point (a poster is a reader too). Two pre-existing tests (channel_ac02, meshops_ac06) were adjusted for this, not regressed.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did read() never see a named channel in the first place?
five_whys_trace.a: read's query joined through groups (JOIN groups g ON g.id = c.group_id) because it was written for PRD-mcphost-agent-channels, which only ever created group channels -- migration 0027's earlier, ungated name-keyed channels (PRD-mcphost-agent-mesh-ops) predate that join and were never retrofitted into it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did post() already handle both kinds but read() didn't?
five_whys_trace.a: post() kept the migration-0027 mesh-ops code path as its own `else` arm alongside the newer group path (two lookups, written at two different times for two different PRDs, never merged); read() was only ever written once, for the group case, so it had no equivalent fallback to fall into.

five_whys_trace.q: Why wasn't the gap caught before the 2026-09-30 dogfood run?
five_whys_trace.a: open(name) -> post -> read is exactly the sequence host.channel.open's own doc comment ("creates the channel if it doesn't already exist, else returns the existing one") tells a caller to use, but no existing test exercised that specific sequence end-to-end across both verbs -- the mesh-ops and agent-channels test suites each proved their own PRD's verbs in isolation.

five_whys_trace.q: Why unify through one resolve_channel instead of just adding a second lookup inside read()?
five_whys_trace.a: freeze/close/unfreeze had the identical gap (group-only reach) for the identical reason -- patching read() alone would have left three more call sites to independently remember to patch the same way, the exact failure mode (a lookup rule duplicated instead of shared) that produced this bug in the first place.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does a named channel's read stay owner-only, or open up to anyone who has ever posted to it (PRD's own technical considerations names both options, drafted 'owner only')?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Owner only, per the PRD's own drafted default -- a non-owner's read gets channel_not_found, not a distinct authorization error, so a miss and an unauthorized hit read identically (the same posture AC2/AC4 already require for a group channel's non-member). Named channels are single-tenant today; broadening this is out of scope (PRD non-goal: no membership changes).

ambiguities_resolved.question: Keep the name-opened channel path (parity) or deprecate it in favor of group channels (PRD's own open question, owner Joe, due 2026-10-08)?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Keep, parity -- the PRD's own TL;DR names this as the drafted default, and the open question's due date (2026-10-08) is after this dispatch's build date; AC6 states both kinds exist and are both readable rather than naming a deprecation. If Joe decides to deprecate later, that is a follow-up PRD, not a revision of this one.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should channel_post's pre-PRD auto-advance of the poster's own cursor survive unification, now that read() can see the poster's own post?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- removed. Auto-advancing on post meant a poster's own next read (cursor already past the post) returned nothing, which is the same bug class this PRD fixes (a channel you can post to, you should be able to read), just one hop later. channel_ac02 and meshops_ac06 were adjusted for this, not regressed; see hard_constraints.additional.
